mapping: Collapsing height to a top-down plane is an orthographic projection: it removes perspective scale ambiguity but flattens occluders into the same footprint.
Voxelising a point cloud is resampling on a uniform grid; point-based sets keep the original, density-varying samples.
Sparse convolution only computes where features exist — a spatial hash of occupied cells — instead of a dense 3D tensor.
LiDAR supplies geometry, cameras supply semantics; fusing them is combining conditionally independent evidence about occupancy.
Set queries attending over features is a differentiable key–value lookup that replaces hand-coded anchors or NMS.
Unwrapping the LiDAR sphere into a 2D range image trades 3D sparsity for a dense image grid, at the cost of scale distortion.
